stem.text: Let \( W(t) = t + 9 \arctan{\left(\frac{2 t}{3} \right)} \) for \( 0 \le t \le 7 \). Using a calculator, find the value of t in the interval \( 3 < t < 6 \) at which the instantaneous rate of change of W equals the average rate of change of W over \( 3 \le t \le 6 \). Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The average rate of change of W over the interval is \( \frac{W(6) - W(3)}{6 - 3} \), which is about 1.656 (more places are kept).
Differentiate: \( W'(t) = 1 + \frac{54}{4 t^{2} + 9} \). Set \( W'(t) \) equal to the average rate of change and solve on \( 3 < t < 6 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: instantaneous rate set equal to the average rate

worked_solution.text: The calculator's solver gives one solution in the interval, \( t = 4.281 \).

options.derivation: the average rate of change rounded to one decimal place before solving
the average rate of change taken over 0 to 6 instead of the stated interval, then solved on that wider interval
W at both endpoints rounded to whole numbers before forming the average rate of change
